body: 2100 Ross Avenue, a 33-story office tower in downtown Dallas's Arts District, was flagged for an October 6, 2026 foreclosure auction, according to The Real Deal, which cited Roddy's Foreclosure Listing Service. The building has about 840,000 square feet. It was built in 1982 and last renovated in 2014.

The tower is owned by Dundon Capital Partners, the firm of Dallas billionaire Thomas Dundon, which allegedly defaulted on a $98 million loan that Wells Fargo made in 2016. Pacific Elm Properties manages the building. The Real Deal noted that the owner could still work out an agreement with the lender before the auction.

The previous owner, Atlanta-based Cousins Properties, bought the tower out of foreclosure in 2012 for $59 million. It renovated the building, leased it to 90 percent occupancy, and sold it to Dundon Capital in 2015 for $131 million, The Real Deal reported, citing The Dallas Morning News.

timeline.label: Cousins Properties buys 2100 Ross Avenue out of foreclosure for $59 million
Cousins sells the tower to Dundon Capital for $131 million
Wells Fargo makes the $98 million loan
Tower is listed for foreclosure by Roddy's Foreclosure Listing Service
Scheduled foreclosure auction date; the result has not been reported
